children: Shares in Next rose Thursday after the retailer hiked guidance for the fiscal year on higher sales expectations.
Shares in early European trade were up 220 pence, or 1.5%, at 14,780 pence, having reached 15,035 pence earlier in the session.
The London-listed company--a bellwether for the U.K. retail sector--said the new guidance stemmed from an upgrade in sales expectations and some additional cost savings, mainly in warehousing.

Next said it now expected full-price sales--a closely watched industry metric--to rise by 6.7% to 6 billion pounds ($8.03 billion). It had previously guided for a 6.3% rise for the year. Group sales growth expectations were also increased to 6.9%, from 6.6%, to 7.5 billion pounds.
As for adjusted pretax profit, this was raised to 1.255 billion pounds from 1.24 billion pounds.

Next also raised international online sales expectations by an extra 40 million pounds, or 20.5%, and said this would offset expectations of a slightly weaker U.K. performance. Next reduced its U.K. sales forecast by 18 million pounds, lowering expected growth to 2.0% from 2.8% as it was concerned about rising inflation, higher mortgage interest costs and a weak employment market.

The company has developed a strong international growth story, which has been driven by women's and menswear, as well as targeted marketing in Europe, the Middle East and the rest of the world, RBC Capital Markets analysts said in a note.
"Next should benefit from further real wage growth in the U.K. albeit it will remain somewhat sensitive to the employment outlook and cost of borrowing for the consumer," the analysts said.

For the six months through July, Next reported a rise in pretax profit to 566 million pounds from 509 million pounds a year earlier. Revenue rose to 3.45 billion pounds from 3.145 billion pounds, beating Visible Alpha consensus of 3.42 billion pounds.
Full-price sales for the first half were up 7.7%, while total sales including markdowns were 8.9% higher.
